name: webgpu-g1-wgsl-validation
title: WebGPU G1: hand-written WGSL for the unlit, lit and text shaders, a parity test against the shared shader interface table, and WGSL validation by Tint and naga in CI
issue: USER DECISIONS (2026-10-20, final, do NOT revisit): the design in C:/Method Notes Obsidian/orchestrator/proposals/webgpu-backend-design.md is accepted with ALL recommendations W1-W10: hand-written WGSL for the three built-in shaders tied to the shared interface table by a parity test and validated by Tint (and naga) in CI (W1); WebGPU goldens run natively on Dawn over lavapipe in a new NON-REQUIRED Linux CI job (W2, G2 and later); one wasm containing both renderers chosen at load (W3); WebGPU is the automatic default when the browser offers it with a ?renderer= override (W4); device loss = one silent re-acquire then a 'continue with software' button (W5); emdawnwebgpu with the device acquired in loader JS before callMain, no ASYNCIFY (W6); devicePixelRatio with a 2560 cap (W7); the native WebGPU backend exists only for the CI harness, option OFF by default, not selectable in lua_project or the editor host (W8); v1 = built-in shaders only, wireframe ignored with one warning, no compute, particles/soft bodies on CPU paths (W9); G0-G2 now, G4 after the stage 5 PR #184 merges (W10). Read C:/Method Notes Obsidian/orchestrator/proposals/webgpu-backend-design.md FULLY (sections 3-7 and the staged plan) before starting. THIS ITEM IS PR G1 and REQUIRES G0 (webgpu-g0-shared-gpu-pieces) TO BE MERGED FIRST (the shared GpuShaderInterface table); do not start the developer until G0 is in master. SCOPE per the design (sections on shader strategy and the G1 row): (1) renderer/shaders/webgpu/{unlit,lit,text}.wgsl hand-written ports of the three built-in shaders (read the Vulkan GLSL shaders and VulkanShaderInterface/GpuShaderInterface to mirror the interface exactly): handle the issues the design lists: row_major matrix blocks (WGSL cannot express them: use the transpose-on-upload convention and document it), lit.vert's inverse() (write an inverse helper in WGSL), combined image samplers (separate texture and sampler bindings), derivatives/uniformity for text and lit (fwidth, textureSample after discard: keep it valid under WGSL uniformity analysis, the CI validator is the proof); (2) a WebGpuShaderParityTests.cpp (a pure text/parse test, no GPU, runs on every leg that runs renderer tests): parses the .wgsl files (bind groups, bindings, struct member offsets/sizes/types) and compares to the shared interface table, and checks every uniform name Material::ApplyUniforms sets exists in the corresponding WGSL; deterministic failure messages naming the file/binding; (3) WGSL VALIDATION IN CI: pick the lightest robust way to run Tint (and naga) on the three files in an existing Linux job or a new small NON-REQUIRED job (state the added minutes): pinned versions with hashes (e.g. prebuilt tint/naga release binaries, or cargo-installed naga-cli with a lockfile/pin, or the Dawn tint target if G2's Dawn is not available yet: justify and pin), the job fails on any validation error or warning-as-error you choose and is documented; do NOT add a required check and do NOT rename existing jobs; docs-only skip pattern must be followed for any new job; (4) embed the WGSL as strings through CMake for later use by the backend (a generated header or a resource library target, native and web safe; nothing links WebGPU yet and N2ENGINE_RENDERER_WEBGPU does not exist yet: do NOT add it); (5) DOCS: a section in the rendering docs (and docs/testing.html) describing the WGSL files, the conventions (transpose-on-upload, separate samplers, inverse helper), the parity test and the validation job, and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES for Tint/naga if you ship or fetch them in CI only (state which); verify against the code. Nothing builds locally; CI is the test; expect fix rounds. Unverified: actual rendering (G2/G3).
acceptance: Three WGSL shaders exist mirroring the shared interface table; conventions documented
Parity test (no GPU) compares WGSL bindings/offsets/uniform names to the table and Material::ApplyUniforms
Tint and naga validate the shaders in CI (non-required job or existing job, pinned, minutes stated)
WGSL embedded for later use; no WebGPU backend/option yet; all 10 checks green; docs verified
notes: Reviewer: WGSL semantics (alignment/std140-vs-WGSL layout rules, matrix transpose convention applied consistently, uniformity of derivatives and sampling, inverse helper correctness, sampler/texture split, depth range and clip-space notes), parity test is meaningful and fails on a mismatch, validator pins and hashes real, CI job not required and follows the docs-only skip, no new required check, docs true.
